title: All About Woodlice
note: b417 — Phase 5 continues (School readiness) — non-fiction, real facts about woodlice.

pages.brief: A small grey woodlouse resting on the flat top of an old stone garden wall.
A close-up of the woodlouse showing its segmented, bumpy grey shell.
An underside view of the woodlouse showing its many small legs.
The woodlouse tightly curled up into a small round ball shape.
The woodlouse tucked into a damp, shadowy crack in the stone wall.
A narrow crack in the wall where several woodlice are tucked in close together.
A woodlouse nibbling at a piece of old, damp, rotting leaf.
Nell the bee hovering just above the wall, looking down at the woodlouse.
Nell the bee watching closely as the woodlouse curls up tight.
Nell the bee and the woodlouse together on the wall top, the garden visible behind them.
